focus: The growth blocker is a THROUGHPUT CEILING, not dedupe and not the publish gate. claim_one_step does 'order by s.id asc ... limit 1' and drains exactly ONE step per worker tick, and the '1m' worker cron (everyMs=60000) is serialized behind its own isolated agentTurn, so its effective tick rate is ~3-5/h, not 60/h. Measured over 12h: 194 step arrivals (16.2/h) vs 51 completions (4.3/h) = net +11.9/h backlog growth. Queue = 312 and growing; oldest queued CONTENT step (93610, write_content) has waited 19.5h; oldest queued step 93603 waited 19.6h. Every content artifact in the company is behind this ceiling. Second, NEW audience-value finding nobody has measured: all 12 authored tweets in the last 24h are about our own internal machinery (11/12 self-only, 1 both, 0 research-only) while 6/11 authored ARTICLES carry the externally-interesting market finding (skills.sh / ClawHub / trust-scanner). Unblock publishing tomorrow and we ship 12 posts about our own queue mechanics with zero audience value. Ship one change - batch the claim (limit 20) and drain in a loop, so throughput is bounded by the DB, not by one-step-per-tick - plus one change - require payload.context to cite the intel artifact filename the draft came from (1/35 authored tweets do today, 34/35 share one identical topic string). Measure in 24h: completions/h >= 16 (from 4.3), queue <= 50 (from 312), oldest queued content step wait < 1h (from 19.5h), and research-referencing share of new authored tweets >= 50% (from 0/12) with payload.context citation on >= 80% (from 1/35). Guardrail: tweet.posted stays 0 and no tweet is published - the social adapter returns mock_<ts> ids, so any posted tweet is fake reach.

MECHANISM: src/lib/db.ts:77 calls rpc claim_one_step; supabase/migrations/002_claim_one_step_fn.sql selects 'where status=queued and run_after <= now() order by s.id asc for update skip locked limit 1'. One claim = one step = one tick. There is no drain loop and no batch size.

MECHANISM 2: the worker cron job d3c1f8f6 'aicompany-worker-1m-isolated' has schedule everyMs=60000 and its own nextRunAtMs = lastRunAtMs+60000, yet the OBSERVED runAtMs deltas across its last 50 runs are 466,984,4030,2014,2326,1122,3456,706,326,3551,4290,957,355,745,395,1636,1531,1679,1218,941,133,60,1472 s - median 1122s (~3.2/h), max 4290s. The 1-minute worker is serialized behind its own isolated agentTurn (observed durationMs 5-28s each, plus scheduling delay), so nominal cadence is not delivered cadence.

Manually ran 'npm run worker:once' 5x back to back: each run claimed exactly ONE step (93597, 93598, 93599, 93600, 93601), all analyze, all succeeded. Confirms one-step-per-tick by direct observation, not inference.

NEW AUDIENCE-VALUE FINDING (no prior scout cycle measured what the drafts are ABOUT, only how many exist): 12 authored tweets (hook+text, non-mock) in the last 24h classify as 11 self-only / 1 self+research / 0 research-only. Self-reference markers hit: our own repo paths, CLAIM_SQL, postmortems, idempotency keys, step counts. The externally-interesting market signal (skills.sh installs frozen at 2026-06-19, trust-scanner mirror divergence, 52 people building the same scanner) lives in the ARTICLES: 6/11 authored articles name a third-party marketplace/scanner (skills.sh, ClawHub), 9/11 are research-flavored.

LINEAGE IS MISSING: only 1 of 35 lifetime authored tweets carries payload.context; 34/35 share the byte-identical topic string 'high-signal company update for audience engagement'. There is no machine-checkable link from intel artifact -> draft -> publish. 11,089 draft_tweet steps exist lifetime but only 35 are authored (hook+text); the other 11,054 are topic-only shells.

MEASUREMENT INFRASTRUCTURE IS ABSENT, so 'publish then measure' is not merely blocked, it is undefined: ops_social_posts has 0 rows, and ops_audience / ops_followers / ops_social_metrics / ops_replies / ops_reaction_queue do not exist as tables at all. Only 5 event kinds exist fleet-wide: content.drafted, insight.generated, proposal.created, step.succeeded, tweet.drafted. tweet.posted = 0 lifetime. There is no follower count, no impression count, no engagement event, so no growth KPI can be computed from this system's own data even after the publish path is fixed.

NO DISTRIBUTION SURFACE EXISTS: the repo ships a Next.js Mission Control app (app/content/page.tsx, app/api/mc/content/route.ts, mc_content table) but mc_content has 0 rows and there is no deploy target (no vercel/netlify/docker/fly config, no public URL in README or env). Discord is configured in openclaw.json and is the only live external channel; the company has never posted to it.

DEFINITION DRIFT in draft metrics: the newest authored tweet (93956, 17:43Z) asserts '12 today, 34 lifetime' real drafts; a strict hook+text filter yields 20 lifetime. Prior cycles reported 32/33/34 for the same corpus under looser filters. There is no shared definition of 'real draft', so different channels quote different numbers for the same corpus.

STALENESS RISK: authored tweets assert live-metric facts with no as-of stamp. Tweet 93815 (08:34Z) claims '93,777 steps'; the table now holds 93,925 (+148). Tweet 93902 claims '11,086 tweets / 11,025 identical'; draft_tweet now 11,089. Publishing these externally would publish stale metrics as current facts.
opportunities: OPPORTUNITY 1 (highest leverage, small scope): raise the drain ceiling instead of reducing arrivals. Change claim_one_step to 'limit 20' and have the worker loop the claim until it returns no row. Throughput stops being a function of agent-turn latency and becomes a function of the DB. One SQL change + one loop, no new tables, no schema migration.

OPPORTUNITY 2 (free): the claim is 'order by s.id asc', so the 284 queued analyze postmortem steps are interleaved with the 28 content steps by id. Ordering by kind priority (draft_tweet/write_content first) or even simply by age-of-need would let the 28 real content steps flush within a single batch of 20-30 claims, without waiting for the 284 duplicates to burn through.

OPPORTUNITY 3 (audience value, unmeasured until now): the research is already strong and externally interesting - 6/11 articles name skills.sh/ClawHub trust-scanner findings, including the frozen install counter (2026-06-19) and 52 third parties building the same scanner. The tweet lane is a pure funnel from that research to an audience and currently carries none of it. Re-anchoring drafts to the research finding costs one brief change, not new research.

OPPORTUNITY 4: Discord is configured, enabled and live - the only real external channel available today - and the company has never posted to it. It is the cheapest possible first audience loop and does not require the X adapter, credentials or the publish path to be unblocked.
OPPORTUNITY 5: the Mission Control web app can host the content as a real page (mc_content exists, 0 rows) - but there is no deploy target, so treat this as a later step, not this cycle.
risks: RISK 1 (highest): publishing without value is worse than not publishing. If the publish gate were opened today, the first 12 posts would be about our own CLAIM_SQL, step counts and postmortems - zero external appeal, and 12 posts is enough to set a low ceiling for the account. Fix the queue first AND the brief, in that order.

RISK 2: publishing stale live metrics. Authored tweets assert step/tweet counts with no as-of timestamp and they are already drifting by ~150 in hours. Externally, a wrong number is a credibility hit that outlasts the post.

RISK 3: metric-definition drift across agents (20 vs 32 vs 34 'real drafts' depending on filter). If two channels publish different counts of the same corpus, the audience will notice and the operator will lose trust in the numbers.
RISK 4: raising the claim limit without a drain guard could starve the DB or let one tick run long; keep the batch modest (20) and keep the per-step work bounded.

RISK 5: if the batch claim prioritizes content kinds, the 284 duplicate analyze postmortems never drain and the queue still grows; the dedupe/root-cause work from cycles 1125Z and 1256Z is still needed, but it is now the SECOND fix, not the first.

RISK 6: no follower/impression/engagement tables exist, so there is still no KPI. Any 'publish and see what happens' plan has nothing to read. The honest near-term metric is publish-queue and audience-value mix, not engagement rate.
next_experiments: EXPERIMENT 1 (ship now, 24h window): batch-claim limit 20 + drain loop in the worker. Success: completions/h >= 16 (from 4.3), queued <= 50 (from 312), oldest queued content step wait < 1h (from 19.5h). Failure signal: queue still growing after 6h.

EXPERIMENT 2 (ship now, 24h window): order the claim to prefer content kinds (draft_tweet, write_content) ahead of analyze. Success: all 28 currently-queued content steps claimed within 2h. This is directly measurable against the known queue snapshot.

EXPERIMENT 3 (ship now, 24h window): add a required payload.context on new draft_tweet steps citing the source intel artifact filename, and a check that rejects a draft whose topic string is the default. Success: payload.context citation rate on new authored tweets >= 80% (from 1/35), and research-referencing share of new authored tweets >= 50% (from 0/12).

EXPERIMENT 4 (measure only, no external action): define one shared 'real draft' predicate (hook AND text AND length >= 40 AND non-mock payload) and stamp every draft with it, so all agents quote the same number. Success: one definition referenced by every role's output; variance across agents = 0.

EXPERIMENT 5 (next cycle, gated): first external post to Discord with a research-derived message, metrics writer enabled. Gated on EXPERIMENT 3 passing and on an explicit human go - the company has zero followers there, so a single research-derived post to a live channel is the smallest honest audience test available. Not to be run in this cycle.
notes: Distinguishes from prior scout cycles on purpose. 0940Z identified the mock-LLM/mock-social adapters as the publish blocker; 1054Z attacked analyze starvation of content steps; 1125Z and 1256Z attacked the dedupe/postmortem arrival tax. None of them measured the drain ceiling itself (arrivals 16.2/h vs completions 4.3/h, one step per claim, effective worker tick ~3-5/h) and none measured audience value of the drafts themselves (0/12 research-referencing in the last 24h despite research-flavored articles sitting right next to them).

Prior cycles were not wrong about the arrival tax - the postmortem flood is real - but suppressing arrivals caps throughput at arrival rate while the ceiling is what gates everything. Fix the ceiling first, the tax second.
